title: RFID & NFC Resource Center — Datasheets, EPC Templates, Artwork & Compliance Downloads
summary: Free, no-form-required downloads that procurement, engineering and brand teams need before placing an RFID or NFC order. Chip datasheets in PDF, GS1 SGTIN-96 encoding templates in Excel, hotel-key-card artwork templates in PDF/AI, DSCSA compliance white papers, NDEF programming cheatsheets, and the Proud Tek sample-pack request brief. Files are version-controlled and refreshed when the underlying chip or regulation changes.
heroPoints: Direct downloads. No gating form, no email signup wall — most procurement teams need these files in their first sprint and we are not in the business of slowing that down.

Thirteen files spanning chip datasheets, GS1 SGTIN-96 encoding templates, hotel key card artwork templates, NDEF programming cheatsheets, DSCSA compliance white papers, the Proud Tek company profile and the sample-pack request brief.
Files carry version numbers + last-reviewed dates so you can re-verify the current revision before a production order.
imageAlt: Laptop, smartphone and notebook on a sunlit wooden desk

brief.label: When to use these files
items: Before requesting a sample pack — read the chip family datasheet first so you can specify the exact part number on the request.
Before encoding a production batch — open the GS1 SGTIN-96 template and pre-allocate the serial-number range so your supplier and DC agree on encoding rules.
Before designing artwork — use the hotel-key-card template so the chip antenna position survives the print bleed.
Before answering an FDA / DSCSA audit — the compliance white paper cites the specific 21 CFR sections and EPCIS event types the auditor will ask about.

brief.label: What is NOT here
items: Production-grade chip datasheets that contain trade-secret information (NXP DESFire EV3 internals, {chip:impinj-m730:name} register maps). Those are NDA-only — request from your Proud Tek specialist.
Brand-locked artwork templates from lock vendors (Saflok / Onity / Salto / VingCard). Those are vendor-issued; we'll point you at the right vendor contact.
Customer-specific files. If your last order had a custom template attached, it stays in your project folder — ask your Proud Tek account manager.

sections.title: Browse the resource library
sections.intro: Thirteen downloads, all current as of June 2026. Each card lists file type, size, version and last-reviewed date.
paragraphs: Files open in your browser; right-click to save. If a file is broken or out of date, ping info@proudtek.com — we'll refresh it within one business day. All PDFs are linearised for in-browser preview; templates ship as XLSX, PDF, AI and ZIP depending on what makes the most sense to edit.

sections.title: Chip family reference cards
sections.intro: One-page or two-page reference cards summarising chip memory, read range, security profile, smartphone compatibility, typical use cases and the closest Proud Tek SKU. Use these to spec the chip family on a request without opening the full datasheet.
bullets: EM4100 / EM4305 / T5577 — LF 125 kHz reference card (2 pp PDF).
MIFARE Classic / Plus / DESFire EV3 — HF 13.56 MHz hotel & access reference card (2 pp PDF).
NTAG213 / 215 / 216 — NFC marketing card reference card (1 pp PDF).
NTAG424 DNA — authenticated NFC + SDM reference card (2 pp PDF).
{chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} / UCODE 8 / 9 / Higgs-9 — UHF RAIN reference card (2 pp PDF).

sections.title: Encoding & artwork templates
sections.intro: Editable templates for the most common encoding and artwork tasks. Open in Excel, Adobe Illustrator or any standard tooling.
bullets: GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC encoding template — XLSX with company-prefix / item-reference / serial-number columns + a 24-bit GS1 prefix calculator.
Hotel key card CMYK artwork template — AI + PDF, 85 × 54 mm bleed-safe, chip antenna position marked, magnetic-stripe omit lane indicated.
Apparel hang-tag inlay placement template — PDF, marks the Monza R6-P antenna footprint so artwork avoids antenna interference.
NDEF record cheatsheet — 1 pp PDF covering URL, vCard, text and launch-app NDEF types with byte-budget tables for NTAG213/215/216.

sections.title: Compliance & buying briefs
sections.intro: Documents your compliance and procurement teams need to keep on file.
bullets: DSCSA item-level RFID compliance brief — PDF, cites 21 CFR Part 121 + the FDA's Lightweight Verification API specification.
EU Digital Product Passport (ESPR) implementation brief — PDF, walks through the 2027 enforcement timeline for batteries, textiles, electronics.
Proud Tek sample-pack request brief — 1 pp PDF describing how to scope a sample pack request for the fastest possible specialist reply.
Proud Tek company profile (2026 edition) — PDF covering the factory, certifications and product families, for supplier-qualification files.

faq.question: Why are the downloads not gated behind a form?
faq.answer: Because the procurement teams that use them have already decided to consider Proud Tek. Gating documentation that helps them spec the right chip just slows their week-1 evaluation. We track downloads in our analytics so we can see which files matter; we do not need your email to do that. If you want to start a specialist conversation, use the sample-pack form or the RFQ wizard — both are voluntary.

faq.question: How often are the files updated?
faq.answer: Chip reference cards are reviewed quarterly and any time the chip vendor publishes a new revision (the NXP NTAG424 DNA SDM specification was last refreshed in March 2026; our reference card carries the corresponding `Last reviewed 2026-04`). Compliance briefs are reviewed any time the underlying regulation changes (FDA published DSCSA Section 582 enforcement guidance in November 2024; the brief was refreshed the following week).

faq.question: Can I redistribute these files?
faq.answer: Yes, internally within your buyer organisation. The files are designed to circulate inside procurement, engineering, design and compliance teams. We ask that you not republish them on a public website — link to this page instead so your readers always get the current revision.

faq.question: I need a file that isn't here. Can you build one?
faq.answer: Often, yes — if it's a procurement-facing template that other buyers will also use. Email info@proudtek.com with the use case and we'll evaluate whether to build it. Customer-specific work (your-artwork, your-SGTIN-prefix) stays in your project folder and not here.
